sentences.zh: 其江乘、攝山、鍾山等諸軍相次克捷，虜蕭軌、東方老、王敬寶、李希光、裴英起等將帥凡四十六人。

translations.literal: The armies at Jiangcheng, Sheshan, Zhongshan, and elsewhere in succession achieved victory; captured were Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, Pei Yingqi, and other generals altogether forty-six men.
translations.idiomatic: Columns at Jiangcheng, Sheshan, Bell Mountain, and the rest won in turn. Among forty-six commanders taken were Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, and Pei Yingqi.

sentences.zh: 其軍士得竄至江者，縛荻筏以濟，中江而溺，流屍至京口，翳水彌岸。

translations.literal: Their soldiers who could flee to the river tied reed rafts to cross; mid-river they drowned; floating corpses reached Jingkou; the water was obscured to the banks.
translations.idiomatic: Those who reached the river lashed reed rafts and drowned midstream; corpses drifted to Jingkou until the water hid the banks.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，红軍出南州，燒賊舟艦。

translations.literal: On dingsi day the army went out from Nan Province and burned the rebels' boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day the imperial troops marched out of Nan Province and burned the rebel fleet.

sentences.zh: 己未，斬劉歸義、徐嗣彥、傅野嚢于建康市。

translations.literal: On jiwei day Liu Guiyi, Xu Siyan, and Fu Yenang were beheaded in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Liu Guiyi, Xu Siyan, and Fu Yenang were executed in the market at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: [22]是日解嚴。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 22. That day martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 22. That day the capital stood down from martial law.

sentences.zh: 庚申，蕭軌、東方老、王敬寶、李希光、裴英起皆伏誅。

translations.literal: On gengshen day Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, and Pei Yingqi all suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, and Pei Yingqi were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 高祖表解南徐州以授侯安都。

translations.literal: The Founder memorialized to relinquish South Xuzhou and grant it to Hou Andu.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder asked leave to give up South Xuzhou and turn it over to Hou Andu.

sentences.zh: 七月景子，詔授高祖中書監、司徒、揚州刺史，進爵為公，增邑赠前五千戶，侍中、使持節、都督中外諸軍事、將軍、尚書令、班闰、鼓吹、甲仗嵭如故，赠給油幢皁輪車。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on jingzi day, an edict appointed the Founder Director of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Yangzhou; advanced his rank to Duke; added to his fief, together with the previous grant, five thousand households; and left unchanged his posts as Palace Attendant, bearer of the staff, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, General, Director of the Masters of Writing, attendance retinue, pipes and drums, armor and weapons, as before—also granting an oil-canopied carriage with black wheels.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jingzi day, an edict named the Founder Director of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and inspector of Yangzhou, raised him to duke, and added five thousand households to his fief on top of what he already held. He kept his palace attendant rank, staff of office, supreme command over all armies, generalship, directorship of the Masters of Writing, guard retinue, pipes and drums, and armor and arms as before, and was given an oil-canopied carriage with black wheels.

sentences.zh: 是月侯瑱以江州入附。

translations.literal: That month Hou Chen submitted Jiang Province in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: That month Hou Chen brought Jiang Province over to the court.

sentences.zh: 遣侯安都鎮上流，定南中諸郡。

translations.literal: Hou Andu was sent to garrison the upper reaches and settle the southern interior commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu was dispatched upstream to pacify the southern interior commanderies.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，太府卿何敳、新州刺史華志各上玉璽一，高祖表以送臺，詔歸之高祖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guimao day, Grand Storehouse Director He Shu and Xin Province Inspector Hua Zhi each presented one jade seal; the Founder memorialized sending them to the terrace; an edict returned them to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guimao day, Grand Storehouse Director He Shu and Xin Province Inspector Hua Zhi each offered a jade seal. The Founder sent them up to the throne; the court ordered them given back to him.

sentences.zh: 是日詔高祖食安吉、武康二縣，合五千戶。

translations.literal: That day an edict granted the Founder the revenue of Anji and Wukang, two counties together totaling five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict assigned him the tax income of Anji and Wukang—five thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，改年曰太平元年。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renyin day, the era name was changed to the first year of Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renyin day, the reign was retitled the first year of Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 進高祖位丞相、錄尚書事、鎮纫大將軍，改刺史為牧，進封義興郡公，侍中、司徒、都督、班闰、鼓吹、甲仗、皁輪車嵭如故。

translations.literal: The Founder was advanced to Chancellor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Pacifying Grand General; the title inspector was changed to governor; he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing commandery; Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, Commander-in-Chief, attendance retinue, pipes and drums, armor and weapons, and the black-wheeled carriage remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to chancellor, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Pacifying Grand General; his Yangzhou post became a governorship; he was made Duke of Yixing. He kept his palace attendant rank, ministry, supreme command, guard retinue, pipes and drums, arms, and black-wheeled carriage unchanged.

sentences.zh: 丁未，中散大夫王彭牋稱今月五日平旦於御路見龍跡，自大社至象闕，异三四里。

translations.literal: On dingwei day Palace Attendant for Scattered Retainers Wang Peng memorialized that on the fifth of this month at dawn he had seen dragon tracks on the imperial road from the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain to the Elephant Gate, strange for three or four li.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Wang Peng, palace attendant for scattered retainers, reported that at dawn on the fifth of the month he had seen dragon tracks along the imperial road from the Grand Altar to the Elephant Gate—a marvel stretching three or four li.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔追贈高祖考侍中、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，封義興郡公，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: On gengshen day an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Founder's father as Palace Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with gold seal and purple sash, as Duke of Yixing, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day an edict posthumously ennobled the Founder's father as palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness, with gold seal and purple sash, Duke of Yixing, posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 十月甲戌，敕丞相自今入問訊，可施別榻以近扆坐。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on jiaxu day, an order said that from now on when the chancellor entered for audience he might use a separate couch placed near the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiaxu day, the throne ordered that when the chancellor came in for audience he might sit on a separate couch beside the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 二年正月壬寅，天子朝萬國於太極東堂，加高祖班闰十人，赠前三十人，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on renyin day, the Son of Heaven received the myriad states at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate's eastern wing; the Founder's attendance retinue was increased by ten, his guard by thirty, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, on renyin day, the emperor received the tribute states in the eastern hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. The Founder's ceremonial retinue was increased by ten and his guard by thirty; everything else stayed as it was.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔贈高祖兄道談散騎常侍、[23]使持節、平北將軍、南论州刺史、長城縣公，謚曰昭烈；

translations.literal: On dingwei day an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Founder's elder brother Daotan as Palace Attendant for Scattered Retainers, Editorial footnote marker 23. bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Governor of Yan Province, and Duke of Changcheng, posthumous name Zhaolie;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day an edict posthumously honored the Founder's elder brother Daotan as palace attendant for scattered retainers, See editorial note 23. bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the North, governor of Yan Province, and Duke of Changcheng, posthumous name Zhaolie;

sentences.zh: 弟休先侍中、使持節、驃騎將軍、南徐州刺史、武康縣侯，[24]謚曰忠壯，食邑各二千戶。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiuxian as Palace Attendant, bearer of the staff, Rapid Tiger General, Governor of South Xuzhou, and Marquis of Wukang, Editorial footnote marker 24. posthumous name Zhongzhuang, each with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Xiuxian as palace attendant, bearer of the staff, Rapid Tiger General, governor of South Xuzhou, and Marquis of Wukang, See editorial note 24. posthumous name Zhongzhuang, each with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: [25]甲寅，遣兼侍中謁者僕射陸繕策拜長城縣夫人章氏為義興國夫人。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 25. On jiayin day the concurrent Palace Attendant and Master of Ceremonial for the Heir Apparent Lu Zhan was sent to invest Lady Zhang of Changcheng as Lady of the State of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 25. On jiayin day Lu Zhan, concurrent palace attendant and master of ceremonies for the heir apparent, was sent to invest Lady Zhang of Changcheng as lady of the state of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔贈高祖祖侍中、太常卿，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: On dingmao day an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Founder's grandfather as Palace Attendant and Minister of Ceremonial, posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict posthumously honored the Founder's grandfather as palace attendant and minister of ceremonial, posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 追封高祖祖母許氏吳郡嘉興縣君，謚曰敬；

translations.literal: The Founder's grandmother Lady Xu was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Jiaxing county, Wu commandery, posthumous name Jing;
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Xu was made Lady of Jiaxing in Wu commandery, posthumous name Jing;

sentences.zh: 妣張氏義興國太夫人，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Zhang as Grand Lady of the State of Yixing, posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: and his mother Lady Zhang as Grand Lady of the State of Yixing, posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 二月庚午，蕭勃舉兵，自廣州渡嶺，頓南康，遣其將歐陽頠、傅泰及其子孜為前軍，[26]至于豫章，分屯要險，南江州刺史余孝頃起兵應勃，高祖命周文育、侯安都率红討平之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengwu day, Xiao Bo raised troops, crossed the ranges from Guangzhou, halted at Nankang, and sent his generals Ouyang Hui, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as the vanguard, Editorial footnote marker 26. reaching Yuzhang and posting troops at strategic passes; South Jiangzhou Inspector Yu Xiaoxiang raised troops in response to Bo; the Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu to lead the army to crush them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu day, Xiao Bo rebelled, crossed the mountains from Guangzhou, and camped at Nankang. He sent Ouyang Hui, Fu Tai, and his son Zi ahead, See editorial note 26. as far as Yuzhang, where they held the passes. Yu Xiaoxiang, inspector of South Jiangzhou, rose to join him. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu with an army to put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，進高祖位太傅，加黃鉞，闰履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，赠給羽葆鼓吹一部，其侍中、都督、錄尚書、鎮纫大將軍、揚州牧、義興郡公、班闰、甲仗、油幢皁輪車嵭如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the Founder was advanced to Grand Tutor, with the yellow battle-axe added, sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hurry in court, and no personal name spoken when he was praised in obeisance; he was also granted one set of feather-canopied pipes and drums; his Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Pacifying Grand General, Governor of Yangzhou, Dukedom of Yixing, attendance retinue, armor and weapons, and oil-canopied carriage with black wheels remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, he was made Grand Tutor and given the yellow battle-axe, the right to wear sword and shoes in the hall, to enter court without hurrying, and to be hailed without his personal name. He received a feather-canopied pipe-and-drum guard. He kept his palace attendant rank, supreme command, recordership, Pacifying Grand General post, Yangzhou governorship, Yixing dukedom, guard retinue, arms, and oil-canopied black-wheeled carriage unchanged.

sentences.zh: 景申，加高祖前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: On jingshen day front and rear feather-canopied pipes and drums were added for the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: On jingshen day he was given feather-canopied pipes and drums for his van and rear as well.

sentences.zh: 是時，湘州刺史王琳擁兵不應命，高祖遣周文育、侯安都率红討之。

translations.literal: At this time Xiang Province Inspector Wang Lin held troops and would not obey orders; the Founder sent Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu leading the army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Lin, inspector of Xiang Province, kept his army and refused orders. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu with troops against him.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinchou day, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinchou day, an edict ran:

sentences.zh: 肇昔元胎剖判，太素氤氳，崇建人皇，必憑洪宰。

translations.literal: In ancient times when the primordial embryo was split apart and the great simplicity was still misty, to raise up the human sovereign one had to rely on a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the world was first cleft from chaos and the great simplicity still hung as mist, to set up the human sovereign always required a great minister at his side.

sentences.zh: 故賢哲之后，牧伯征于四方，神武之君，大監治乎萬國。

translations.literal: Therefore after worthy sages, regional lords were commissioned in the four quarters; among divinely martial rulers, a great overseer governed the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: After the sage kings came, lords were sent to rule the four quarters; under the most martial emperors, a great overseer governed all beneath heaven.

sentences.zh: 又有一匡九合，渠門之賜以隆，戮帶圍溫，行宮之寵斯茂，時危所以貞固，運泰所以光熙，斯乃千載同風，百王不刊之道也。

translations.literal: Again there were those who with one correction united the realm—at the Gate of the Canal the gift was made lofty; who with girdle slain and girdle warmed won the favor of the traveling palace—so in peril the steadfast are proven, in prosperity the bright shine forth: this is the same wind for a thousand ages, the unchanging way of a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: There were also those who with a single stroke set the realm right—the gift at the Canal Gate was raised high; who slew the girdle and warmed the girdle won favor in the traveling palace. In danger the loyal stand firm; in good fortune they shine the brighter. That is the wind that blows alike through a thousand ages, the way no king may set aside.

sentences.zh: 太傅義興公，允文允武，迺聖迺神，固天生德，康濟黔首。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Duke of Yixing, is accomplished in letters and martial in deed, sage and divine; by nature endowed with virtue, he brings peace to the black-headed people.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, Duke of Yixing, is learned and warlike, sage and divine; heaven-born in virtue, he gives peace to the common people.

sentences.zh: 昔在休期，早隆朝寄，遠踰滄海，大極交、越。

translations.literal: Long ago in a time of repose he was early entrusted by the court; he went far beyond the blue sea and joined Jiao and Yue to the great pole.
translations.idiomatic: In days of peace he was early given the court's trust; he crossed the southern sea and bound Jiao and Yue to the imperial center.

sentences.zh: [27]皇運不造，書契未聞，中國其亡，兵凶總至，哀哀唣類，譬彼窮牢，悠悠上天，莫云斯極。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 27. The imperial fortune was unmade; the written covenant went unheard; within China it was perishing; the omens of war gathered; the people wailed; they were like prisoners in a ruined pen; high heaven hung far off, and none could say where the limit lay.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 27. Then the dynasty's fortune broke; the written covenant was never heard; China itself seemed lost; the signs of war piled up; the people wailed like captives in a broken fold; heaven stood far off, and no one could see an end.

sentences.zh: 否終則泰，元輔應期，救此將崩，援茲已溺，乘舟履輂，架險浮深，經略中途，畢殲戝醜。

translations.literal: When obstruction ends, peace comes; the chief minister answered the age; he rescued what was about to collapse and pulled back what had already drowned; riding boats and treading chariots, bridging peril and floating the deep, he campaigned midway and utterly destroyed the rebel host.
translations.idiomatic: When the worst had passed, peace returned; the chief minister met the hour; he saved what was falling and pulled back what had sunk; by boat and chariot, over bridges of peril and across the deep, he fought through the heartland until the rebel host was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 洎乎石頭、姑熟，流髓履腸，一朝指撝，六合清晏。

translations.literal: By the time of Stone City and Gushu, marrow flowed and entrails trailed; with one gesture of command the six quarters were cleared and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: At Stone City and Gushu marrow ran and guts littered the ground; at a single command the six quarters were cleared and stilled.

sentences.zh: 是用光昭下武，翼亮中都，雪三后之勍讎，夷三靈之巨慝。

translations.literal: Therefore he brightly illumined the martial successor, winged the radiance of the central capital, avenged the fierce wrongs of the three queens, and swept away the great evils of the three spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he lit the martial heir, steadied the brilliance of the central capital, avenged the fierce wrongs done the three queens, and swept away the great evils of the three spirits.

sentences.zh: 堯台禹佐，未始能階，殷相周師，固非云擬。

translations.literal: The terrace of Yao and the assistant of Yu never rose so high; the minister of Yin and the teacher of Zhou are not to be named in the same breath.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of Yao and Yu never climbed so high; the counselors of Yin and Zhou are not fit to be named beside him.

sentences.zh: 重之以屯剝餘象，荊楚大崩，天地無心，乘輿委御，五胡荐食，競謀諸夏，八方缱跱，莫有匡救，彊臣放命，黜我沖人，顧影於荼孺之魂，甘心於甯卿之辱。

translations.literal: Added to this were the remaining signs of overthrow and collapse; Jing and Chu fell in ruin; heaven and earth had no heart; the imperial carriage was cast aside; the five barbarians pressed in to devour; they contended for the Chinese realm; the eight directions were bound in knots and none could set things right; powerful ministers defied orders and deposed our young sovereign; he could only gaze on the soul of the infant lord of Zhou and willingly bear the shame of Ning Qing.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that came the last signs of ruin: Jing and Chu collapsed; heaven and earth seemed heartless; the imperial carriage was abandoned; the five barbarians pressed in to devour the land; they fought over China; the eight directions were tied in knots and no one could save them; great ministers defied the throne and cast down our young emperor; he could only look upon the infant lord's ghost and swallow the shame of Ning Qing.

sentences.zh: 劔桉下髻，求哀之路莫從，竊鈇逃責，容身之地無所。

translations.literal: With sword at the neck and hair bound, the road of pleading had no way through; stealing axes and fleeing blame, there was nowhere to hide the body.
translations.idiomatic: Sword at the throat and hair bound, there was no road of appeal; stealing the axe and fleeing blame, there was nowhere left to hide.

sentences.zh: 公神兵奄至，不日清澄，惟是孱蒙，再膺天錄。

translations.literal: The Duke's divine troops came in a rush; in no day all was cleared; only I, feeble and ignorant, again received heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's divine army came like a storm; in less than a day all was cleared; and I, feeble and ignorant, received heaven's mandate once more.

sentences.zh: 斯又巍巍蕩蕩，無德而稱焉。

translations.literal: This again is vast and boundless—there is no virtue by which to name it.
translations.idiomatic: That too is vast beyond naming—no virtue can compass it.

sentences.zh: 加以仗茲忠義，屠彼祅逆，震部夷氛，稽山罷祲，番禺、蠡澤，北鄙西郊，殲厥凶徒，罄無遺種。

translations.literal: Added to this, trusting in loyalty and righteousness, he slaughtered those demonic rebels; he shook away the barbarian miasma of the Zhen region and ended the evil omens at Mount Kuaiji; at Panyu and Lize, in the northern marches and western suburbs, he destroyed the wicked bands until not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, leaning on loyalty and righteousness, he cut down demonic rebels; he shook the barbarian miasma from the Zhen region and ended the evil omens at Kuaiji; at Panyu and Lize, in the northern marches and western suburbs, he destroyed the wicked until none were left.

sentences.zh: 斯則兆民之命，脩短所縣，率土之基，興亡是賴。

translations.literal: Thus the lives of the myriad people—long or short—hang upon him; the foundation of all within the seas—rise or fall—depends upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the lives of the myriad people, long or short, hang upon him; the foundation of all within the seas, rise or fall, depends upon him.

sentences.zh: 於是刑禮兼訓，沿革有章，中外成平，遐邇寧一，用能使陽光合魄，曜象呈暉，棲閣遊庭，抱仁含信，宏勳該於厚地，大道格于玄天。

translations.literal: Thereupon punishments and rites were taught together; institutions had their rules; within and without were at peace; far and near were united as one—so that the yang light joined the moon's brilliance, bright emblems showed their radiance, birds rested in the courtyard galleries, embracing benevolence and holding faith; his great merit covered the thick earth and the great Way reached the dark heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Then punishments and rites were taught together, institutions took their proper form, within and without were at peace, and far and near were one—so that sun and moon shared their light, bright signs shone forth, birds rested in the palace galleries bearing benevolence and faith; his great merit covered the thick earth and the great Way reached the dark heaven.

sentences.zh: 羲、農、炎、昊以來，卷領垂衣之世，聖人濟物，未有如斯者也。

translations.literal: From Fu Xi, Shen Nong, Yan Di, and Hao Xu onward, in ages when the ruler held the scroll and let his robes fall, no sage who succored the people has been like this.
translations.idiomatic: From Fu Xi, Shen Nong, the Flame Emperor, and the Yellow Lord onward, in every age of rule by scroll and trailing robe, no sage who succored the people has matched this.

sentences.zh: 夫備物典策，桓、文是膺，助理陰陽，蕭、曹不讓，未有功高於驱縣，而賞薄於伊、周，凡厥人祇，固懷延佇。

translations.literal: To prepare the regalia and codify the mandate—Huan and Wen received it; to assist yin and yang—Xiao and Cao did not yield; yet never was merit higher than rushing in service while reward was thinner than for Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; all the people surely harbor long expectation.
translations.idiomatic: To ready the regalia and codify the mandate was the portion of Huan and Wen; to assist yin and yang, Xiao and Cao did not yield place—yet never was service greater than his while reward was slighter than Yi Yin's or the Duke of Zhou's; all the people surely wait in hope.

sentences.zh: 寔由公謙撝自牧，降損為懷，嘉數遲回，永言增歎。

translations.literal: Truly because the Duke in humility restrains himself and lowers his person in thought, the fine tally lingers and long sighs are added.
translations.idiomatic: Truly it is because the Duke restrains himself in humility and lowers his person in thought that the fine tally is delayed and sighs grow long.

sentences.zh: 豈可申茲雅尚，久廢朝猷，宜戒司勳，敬升鴻典。

translations.literal: How can this lofty virtue be asserted and court design long left idle? The Director of Merit should be warned to reverently raise the great statute.
translations.idiomatic: How can such lofty virtue be left unhonored and court design long idle? Let the Director of Merit be charged to raise the great statute in reverence.

sentences.zh: 且重華大聖，媯汭惟賢，盛德之祀無忘，公侯之門必復。

translations.literal: Moreover the great sage of Chonghua—at Guirui only the worthy were chosen; the sacrifices of great virtue must not be forgotten; the gate of duke and marquis must be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The great sage Chonghua chose the worthy at Guirui; the rites of great virtue must not be forgotten; the gate of duke and marquis must be opened again.

sentences.zh: 是以殷嘉亶甫，繼后稷之官，堯命羲和，纂重黎之位。

translations.literal: Therefore Yin praised Danfu and continued Hou Ji's office; Yao appointed Xi and He to inherit Chong Li's post.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yin praised Danfu and continued Hou Ji's office; Yao appointed Xi and He to inherit Chong Li's post.

sentences.zh: 況其本枝攸建，宜誓山河者乎？

translations.literal: How much more when his own branch is established—should he not swear the covenant of river and mountain?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when his own house is founded—should he not swear the covenant of river and mountain?

sentences.zh: 其進公位相國，總百揆，封十郡為陳公，備九錫之禮，加璽紱、遠遊冠、綠綟綬，位在諸侯王上，其鎮纫大將軍、揚州牧如故。

translations.literal: Let him be advanced to Chancellor of State, head of the hundred officials, enfeoffed as Duke of Chen over ten commanderies, granted the full rites of the Nine Bestowals, with seal ribbon, far-wandering cap, and green sash added; his rank shall be above all princes and kings; his Pacifying Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou shall remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be raised to chancellor of state, head of the hundred officials, enfeoffed as Duke of Chen over ten commanderies, and granted the full Nine Bestowals, with seal ribbon, far-wandering cap, and green sash; his rank shall stand above all princes and kings; he shall keep his Pacifying Grand General post and Yangzhou governorship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 策曰：

translations.literal: The investiture document said:
translations.idiomatic: The investiture document read:

sentences.zh: 大哉乾元，資日月以貞觀，至哉坤元，憑山川以載物。

translations.literal: Great is the Qian origin, sustaining sun and moon for constant observation; utmost is the Kun origin, bearing mountains and rivers to carry the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Great is the origin of Qian, sustaining sun and moon for the constant gaze; utmost is the origin of Kun, bearing mountains and rivers to carry the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 故惟天為大，陟配者欽明，惟王建國，翼輔者齊聖。

translations.literal: Therefore only heaven is great—he who ascends to match it is reverently bright; only the king establishes the state—he who wings it is equal in holiness.
translations.idiomatic: Only heaven is great, and he who rises to match it is reverently bright; only the king founds the state, and he who wings it is equal in holiness.

sentences.zh: 是以文、武之佐，磻磎蘊其玉璜，堯、舜之臣，榮河鏤其金版。

translations.literal: Thus the assistants of Wen and Wu hid their jade scepters at Panxi; the ministers of Yao and Shun carved their golden tablets at Glory River.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the aides of Wen and Wu hid jade scepters at Panxi; the ministers of Yao and Shun carved golden tablets at Glory River.

sentences.zh: 況乎體得一之鴻姿，寧陽九之危厄，拯橫流於碣石，撲燎火於崑岑，驅馭於韋、彭，跨蹍於齊、晉，神功行而靡用，聖道運而無名者乎？

translations.literal: How much more one whose form holds the unity of the great swan, who calms the peril of the yang ninth, who rescues the cross-flow at Jieshi and beats out the blaze-fire at Kunlun, who drives before him Wei and Peng and tramples Qi and Jin—whose divine merit moves yet is not employed, whose holy way runs yet has no name?
translations.idiomatic: How much more one who embodies the unity of the great swan, who stills the peril of the ninth yang, who rescues the cross-flow at Jieshi and beats out the blaze at Kunlun, who drives Wei and Peng before him and tramples Qi and Jin—whose divine merit moves yet goes unused, whose holy way runs yet bears no name?

sentences.zh: 今將授公典策，其敬聽朕命：

translations.literal: Now I shall confer upon the Duke the canonical document; reverently hear my command:
translations.idiomatic: Now I confer upon the Duke the canonical document. Hear my command in reverence:

sentences.zh: 日者昊天不弔，鍾亂于我國家，網漏吞舟，彊胡內贔，茫茫宇宙，惵惵黎元，方足圓顱，萬不遺一，太清否亢，橋山之痛已深，大寶屯如，平陽之禍相繼。

translations.literal: Lately high heaven did not pity; disorder struck our state; the net leaked and swallowed the boat; strong barbarians grew fierce within; the vast universe, the trembling black-headed people—of round heads and square feet, not one in ten thousand was spared; the Great Clarity was blocked and the pain at Bridge Mountain was already deep; the great treasure was hard pressed and the disaster at Pingyang followed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Lately heaven did not pity us; disorder struck the state; the net tore and the great fish escaped; strong barbarians raged within; in the vast universe the people trembled—of all who walked the earth, not one in ten thousand was spared; the Great Clarity was blocked and grief at Bridge Mountain ran deep; the great treasure was beset and disaster at Pingyang followed close behind.

sentences.zh: 上宰膺運，康救兆民，鞠旅於滇池之南，揚旌於桂嶺之北，懸三光於已墜，謐四海於戝飛，屠猰窳於中原，斮鯨鯢於濛汜。

translations.literal: The chief minister answered the fortune, brought peace to the myriad people, drilled troops south of Lake Dian, raised banners north of Gui Ridge, hung the three lights where they had fallen, stilled the four seas where they flew in rebellion, slaughtered the owl-demon in the central land, and cut the whale in the misty ford.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister met the hour, saved the myriad people, drilled troops south of Lake Dian, raised banners north of Gui Ridge, hung up the three lights where they had fallen, and stilled the four seas in revolt; he slaughtered the owl-demon in the central land and cut the whale in the misty ford.

sentences.zh: 蕩寧上國，光啟中興。

translations.literal: He swept and settled the upper state and brightly opened the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He swept the upper realm clean and brightly opened the restoration.

sentences.zh: 此則公之大造於皇家者也。

translations.literal: This then is the Duke's great creation for the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Duke's great creation for the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 既而天未悔禍，夷醜荐臻，南夏崩騰，西京蕩覆，戝胡孔熾，藉亂乘間，推納藩枝，盜假神器，僴司昏橈，旁引寇讎，既見貶於桐宮，方謀危於漢閣，皇運已殆，何殊贅旒，中國搖然，非徒如悋。

translations.literal: Thereafter heaven did not yet repent the calamity; barbarian fiends pressed in again; South Xia surged in collapse; the western capital was overthrown; rebel barbarians burned bright; seizing disorder they took their chance; they pushed in branch princes and stole the sacred vessel; the usurper minister darkened the rudder and drew in enemy foes by the side; already degraded to the Tung Palace, they then plotted peril for the Han gate; the imperial fortune was already in peril—how different from a dangling tassel; China shook—more than a tottering tile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet heaven had not yet turned from the calamity; barbarian fiends pressed in again; the south collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was overthrown; rebel barbarians flared bright, seizing chaos for their chance; they pushed in princes of the blood and stole the sacred vessel; the usurper minister darkened the helm and drew enemies in at his side; already cast down to the Tung Palace, they then plotted peril at the Han gate; the imperial fortune was at the edge—no mere dangling tassel; China shook—worse than a tottering tile.

sentences.zh: 公赫然投袂，匡救本朝，復莒齊都，平戎王室。

translations.literal: The Duke in majesty flung up his sleeves, rescued and righted the native dynasty, restored Ju for Qi's capital, and pacified the Rong for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke in majesty flung up his sleeves, rescued and righted the native dynasty, restored Ju for Qi's capital, and pacified the Rong for the royal house.

sentences.zh: 朕所以還膺寶歷，重履宸居，挹建武之風猷，个宣王之雅頌。

translations.literal: Therefore I again received the precious succession, again tread the imperial seat, drew in the wind of Jianwu, and recounted and proclaimed the odes of King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I again received the precious succession and again took the imperial seat, drew in the wind of Jianwu, and recounted and proclaimed the odes of King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 此又公之再造於皇家者也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's second creation for the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's second creation for the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 公應務之初，登庸惟始，三川五嶺，莫不窺臨，銀洞珠宮，所在寧謐。

translations.literal: When the Duke first took up affairs and first entered office, the Three Rivers and Five Ridges—none did he not look upon; silver caves and pearl palaces—wherever he went, peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke first took up affairs and first entered office, of the Three Rivers and Five Ridges there was none he did not survey; silver caves and pearl palaces—wherever he went, peace followed.

sentences.zh: 孫、盧肇釁，越貊為災，番部阽危，勢將淪殄。

translations.literal: Sun and Lu began strife; the Yue Mo became disaster; the southern tribes were on the brink and about to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and Lu began strife; the Yue Mo became disaster; the southern tribes teetered on the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 公赤旗所指，祅壘洞開，白羽纔撝，凶徒粉潰。

translations.literal: Where the Duke's red banner pointed, demonic ramparts split open; where the white plume was barely waved, wicked bands crumbled to dust.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Duke's red banner pointed, demonic ramparts split open; where the white plume barely stirred, wicked bands crumbled to dust.

sentences.zh: 非其神武，久喪南藩。

translations.literal: Were it not for his divine martial, the southern marches would long have been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Without his divine martial power, the southern marches would long have been lost.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 大同之末，邊政不脩，李賁狂迷，竊我交、愛，敢稱大號，驕恣甚於尉他，據有連州，雄豪熾於梁碩。

translations.literal: At the end of Great Unity, frontier government was not kept in repair; Li Ben ran mad and stole our Jiao and Ai, dared to take a great title, was more arrogant than Wei Tuo, held a chain of prefectures, and blazed more fiercely than Liang Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Great Unity the frontier was neglected; Li Ben ran mad, seized our Jiao and Ai, dared to take a royal title, outdid Wei Tuo in arrogance, held a chain of prefectures, and burned hotter than Liang Shuo.

sentences.zh: 公英优雄筭，電掃風行，馳御樓船，直跨滄海，新昌、典澈[28]，備履艱難，蘇歷、嘉寧，盡為京觀。

translations.literal: The Duke with heroic stratagem swept like lightning and wind, drove tower ships and crossed the blue sea straight; Xinchang and Dianche, Editorial footnote marker 28. all the hardship was endured; Suli and Jianing were wholly made into victory mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke with heroic stratagem swept like lightning and wind, drove tower ships and crossed the blue sea; at Xinchang and Dianche, See editorial note 28. every hardship was borne; Suli and Jianing were wholly heaped into victory mounds.

sentences.zh: 三山獠洞，八角蠻陬，逖矣水寓之鄉，悠哉火山之國，馬援之所不屆，陶璜之所未聞，莫不懼我王靈，爭朝邊候，歸賝天府，獻狀鴻臚。

translations.literal: The liao caves of Three Mountains and the barbarian corners of Eight Angles—far is the land of water dwellings, long the nation of fire mountains; where Ma Yuan never arrived, where Tao Huang never heard—none did not fear our kingly awesomeness, contend to attend the frontier post, return tribute to the heavenly storehouse, and present registers to the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: The liao caves of Three Mountains and the barbarian corners of Eight Angles—far lie the water dwellings, long the fire mountains; where Ma Yuan never came, where Tao Huang never heard—none failed to fear our kingly awesomeness, strive to attend the frontier post, send tribute to the heavenly storehouse, and present registers to the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 自寇虜陵江，宮闈幽辱。

translations.literal: From the time the bandit foe overran the Yangzi, the palace quarters suffered dark insult.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the bandit foe overran the Yangzi, the palace quarters suffered dark insult.

sentences.zh: 公枕戈嘗膽，提闰拊心，氣涌青霄，神飛紫闥。

translations.literal: The Duke slept on his spear and tasted gall, took his guard in hand and beat his breast; his spirit surged to the blue sky and flew to the purple gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke slept on his spear and tasted gall, took his guard in hand and beat his breast; his spirit surged to the blue sky and flew to the purple gate.

sentences.zh: 而番禺連率，本自諸夷，言得其朋，是懷同惡。

translations.literal: The Panyu commander-in-chief was by origin of the various Yi; when words won him comrades, he cherished the same evil.
translations.idiomatic: The Panyu commander-in-chief was by origin one of the Yi peoples; when words won him allies, he cherished the same evil.

sentences.zh: 公仗此忠誠，乘機勦定，執沛令而釁鼓，平新野而據鞍。

translations.literal: Trusting in this loyalty, the Duke seized the moment to crush and settle them; he seized the Pei magistrate and beat the war drums, pacified Xinye and held the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in this loyalty, the Duke seized the moment to crush and settle them; he seized the magistrate of Pei and beat the war drums, pacified Xinye and held the saddle.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 世道初艱，方隅多難，勳門桀黠，作亂衡嶷，兵切池隍，红兼夷獠。

translations.literal: When the age was first hard and the regions many in difficulty, fierce men of merit gates made rebellion on Mount Heng; soldiers pressed the moats and ponds; the army included the Yi liao.
translations.idiomatic: When the age was first hard and the regions troubled, fierce men of merit houses rebelled on Mount Heng; soldiers pressed the moats and ponds; the army included the Yi liao.

sentences.zh: 公以國盜邊警，知無不為，卹是同盟，誅其醜類，莫不魚驚鳥散，面縛頭懸。

translations.literal: The Duke, because the state was robbed and the frontier alarmed, knew nothing he would not do; he soothed the allied states and executed their ugly kind; none but were startled like fish and scattered like birds, bound with face to the fore and heads hung up.
translations.idiomatic: Because the state was robbed and the frontier alarmed, the Duke left nothing undone; he soothed the allied states and executed their ugly kind until all were startled like fish and scattered like birds, bound with faces to the fore and heads hung up.

sentences.zh: 南土黔黎，重保蘇息。

translations.literal: The black-headed people of the southern land again secured rest and breath.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the southern land again secured rest and breath.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 長驅嶺嶠，夢想京畿，緣道酋豪，遞為榛梗，路養渠率，全據大都，蓄聚逋逃，方謀阻亂，百樓不戰，雲梯之所未窺，萬弩齊張，高輣之所非敵。

translations.literal: Long driving the mountain ranges, he dreamed of the capital region; along the road the tribal chiefs in succession became brambles and barriers; Lu Yangqu led the command and wholly held the great metropolis; he gathered runaways and was just plotting obstruction and disorder; a hundred towers did not fight—what cloud ladders had not yet spied; ten thousand crossbows together drew—what high ramparts they could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Long driving the mountain ranges, he dreamed of the capital; along the road tribal chiefs in turn became brambles and barriers; Lu Yangqu held command and wholly possessed the great metropolis; he gathered fugitives and plotted obstruction and disorder; a hundred towers would not yield—no cloud ladder had yet spied them; ten thousand crossbows drew as one—no high rampart could stand before them.

sentences.zh: 公龍驤虎步，[29]嘯吒風雲，山靡堅城，野無彊陣，清祅氛於灨石，滅沴氣於雩都。

translations.literal: The Duke with dragon stride and tiger step, Editorial footnote marker 29. roaring at wind and cloud, made mountains crumble and strong walls, the wilds without a stubborn formation; he cleared demonic miasma at Ganshi and extinguished evil vapor at Yudu.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke with dragon stride and tiger step, See editorial note 29. roaring at wind and cloud, made mountains crumble and strong walls fall, the wilds without a stubborn line; he cleared demonic miasma at Ganshi and extinguished evil vapor at Yudu.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 遷仕凶慝，屯據大奛，乞活類馬騰之軍，流民多杜弢之红，推鋒轉岗，自北徂南，頻歲稽誅，寔惟勍虜。

translations.literal: Qian Shi, a vicious criminal, held fast at Da Ao; the army begging life resembled Ma Teng's host; the floating people were many like Du Tao's troops; they pushed the spearhead and turned the hill, from north toward south; year after year they were punished—truly a fierce foe.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Shi, a vicious outlaw, held Da Ao; his host of desperate men rivaled Ma Teng's bands, his drifting multitudes Du Tao's troops; they drove the spearhead and wheeled through the hills from north to south; year on year the court struck at them—yet they were a fierce foe indeed.

sentences.zh: 公坐揮三略，遙制六奇，義勇同心，貔貅騁力，雷奔電擊，谷靜山空，列郡無犬吠之驚，叢祠罷狐鳴之盜。

translations.literal: The Duke sat wielding the three stratagems and controlled the six wonders from afar; righteous courage shared one heart; the pixiu exerted their strength; thunder rushed and lightning struck; valleys were still and mountains empty; the commanderies had no alarm of dogs barking; the clustered shrines ceased the fox-cry robbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke sat with the three stratagems in hand and the six wonders at his command; loyal valor moved as one; his shock troops threw their full strength; thunder rushed and lightning struck until valleys fell silent and mountains emptied; no district heard the dog's bark of alarm; the hill shrines went still of fox-fire robbers.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 王師討虜，次屆淪波，兵乏兼儲，士有飢色。

translations.literal: The royal army attacked the bandit foe and next reached the sunken waves; weapons lacked double stores and the soldiers had the color of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The royal army attacked the bandit foe and next reached the sunken waves; weapons lacked double stores and the soldiers wore hunger on their faces.

sentences.zh: 公回麾蠡澤，積穀巴丘，億庾之詠斯豐，壺漿之迎是红，軍民轉漕，曾無砥柱之難，艫舳相望，如運敖倉之府，犀渠貝冑，顧蔑雷霆，高艦層樓，仰捫霄漢，故使三軍勇銳，百戰無前，承此兵糧，遂殄凶逆。

translations.literal: The Duke turned his banner at Lize, piled grain at Baqiu; the ode of the hundred thousand granaries was rich; the welcome of pot and drink was the army; military and civil transport by water never knew the difficulty of the pillar stone; ships and boats looked upon one another like moving the storehouse of Ao; rhinoceros channels and shell armor disdained thunder; high ships and layered towers touched the sky; therefore the three armies were brave and sharp, a hundred battles without a forebear; relying on this army grain, they then destroyed the vicious rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke turned his banner at Lize and piled grain at Baqiu until the ode of the hundred thousand granaries rang full; pots and drink lined the army's road; grain moved by water without the pillar stone's hazard; ships passed like shuttling Ao's storehouse; rhinoceros channels and shell armor disdained thunder; high ships and tiered towers scraped heaven—so the three armies grew fierce and unbeaten; on that grain they destroyed the vicious rebels.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 若夫英圖邁俗，義旅如雲，湓壘猜攜，用淹戎略。

translations.literal: As for heroic design surpassing custom, righteous hosts like clouds—at Pen rampart suspicion and division delayed the military plan.
translations.idiomatic: As for heroic design surpassing custom and righteous hosts like clouds—at Pen rampart suspicion and division delayed the military plan.

sentences.zh: 公志唯同嚔，師克在和，鵠塞非虞，鴻門是會，若晉侯之誓白水，如蕭王之推赤心，屈禮交盟，人祗感咽，故能使舟師嵭路，遠邇朋心。

translations.literal: The Duke's will was only to share the same breath; the army overcame through harmony; the swan pass was not feared; the Hong Gate was the meeting—like the Jin marquis swearing at White Water, like the King of Xiao pushing the red heart; bowing in rite and joining in alliance, men and spirits were moved to sigh—therefore the naval army kept the road and far and near shared one heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's will was only to share the same breath; the army overcame through harmony; the swan pass was not feared; the Hong Gate was the meeting—like the Jin marquis swearing at White Water, like the King of Xiao offering the red heart; bowing in rite and joining alliance, men and spirits sighed with feeling—so the naval army held the road and far and near shared one heart.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 姑熟襟要，崤函阻憑，寇虜據其關梁，大盜負其扃鐍。

translations.literal: Gushu was the throat of the pass; Xiaohan was the barrier of the defile; the bandit foe held its gates and bridges; great robbers bore its bolts and bars.
translations.idiomatic: Gushu was the throat of the pass; Xiaohan was the barrier of the defile; the bandit foe held its gates and bridges; great robbers bore its bolts and bars.

sentences.zh: 公一校裁撝，三雄嵭奮，左賢、右角，沙潰土崩，木甲殪於中原，观裘赴於江水，他他藉藉，萬計千戝，鄂啬之隘斯開，夷庚之道無塞。

translations.literal: With one command the Duke judged and directed; the three heroes together exerted themselves; left worthy and right horn—sand collapsed and earth crumbled; wooden armor perished in the central land; barbarian fur went to the river waters; they pressed and pressed—myriad plans and thousand rebels; the narrow pass of Ese was opened; the road of Yigeng was unblocked.
translations.idiomatic: With one command the Duke judged and directed; the three heroes strove together; left worthy and right horn—sand collapsed and earth crumbled; wooden armor perished in the central land; barbarian fur went to the river waters; they pressed and pressed—myriad plans and thousand rebels; the narrow pass of Ese was opened; the road of Yigeng was unblocked.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
translations.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 義軍大红，俱集帝京，逆豎凶徒，猶屯皇邑。

translations.literal: The righteous army's great troops all gathered at the imperial capital; the rebellious wicked and vicious bands still encamped in the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous army's great host gathered at the imperial capital; the rebellious wicked and vicious bands still encamped in the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 若夫表裏山河，金湯嶮固，疏龍首以抗殿，揃華岳以為城，雜虜憑焉，彊兵自若。
公回茲地軸，抗此天羅，曾不崇朝，俾無遺唣，軍容甚穆，國政方脩，物重轨於衣冠，民還瞻於禮樂，楚人滿道，爭轨於葉公，漢老銜悲，俱歡於司隸。
此又公之功也。
內難初靜，諸侯出關，外郡傳烽，鮮卑犯塞，莫非且渠、當戶，中貴名王，冀馬迾於淮南，胡笳動於徐北。
公舟師步甲，异野橫江，殲厥戝羝，遂殫封狶，莫不絓木而止，戎車靡遺，遇濘而旋，歸驂盡殪。
此又公之功也。
公克黜禍難，劬勞皇室，而孫甯之黨，翻啟狄心，伊、洛之閒，咸為虜戍，雖金陵佳氣，石壘天嚴，朝闇戎塵，夜喧胡鼓。
公三籌既畫，八陣斯張，裁舉靈
[⓪]，[30]亦抽金僕，咸俘醜類，悉反高墉，異李廣之皆誅，同龐元之盡赦。
此又公之功也。
任約叛換，梟聲不悛，戎羯貪婪，狼心無改，穹廬氈幕，抵北闕而為營，烏孫天馬，指東都而成陣。
公左甄右落，箕張翼舒，掃是攙槍，驅其獫狁，長狄之種埋於國門，椎髻之酋烹於軍市，投秦坑而盡沸，噎
[濉]水而不流。
[31]此又公之功也。
一相居中，自折彝鼎，五湖小守，妄懷同惡。
公夙駕兼道，衣製杖戈，玉斧將揮，金鉦且戒，祅酋震懾，遽請灰釘，爇櫬以表其含弘，焚書以安其反側。
此又公之功也。
賊龕凶橫，陵虐具區，阻兵安忍，憑災怙亂，自古蟲言鳥跡，渾沌洪荒，凡或虔劉，未此殘酷。
公雖宗居汝潁，世寓東南，育聖誕賢之鄉，含章挺生之地，眷言桑梓，公私憤切，卓爾英狀，[32]丞規奉筭，戮此大憝，如烹小鮮。
此又公之功也。
亂離永久，戝盜孔多，浙左凶渠，連兵構逆，豈止千兵、五校、白雀、黃龍而已哉！
公以中軍無率，選是親賢，奸寇途窮，漼然冰泮，刑溏又作「唐」之所，文命動其大威，雷門之閒，句踐行其嚴戮，英規聖跡，異代同風。
此又公之功也。
同姓有扈，頑凶不賓，憑藉宗盟，圖危社稷，觀兵匯澤，勢震京師，驅率南蠻，已為東帝。
公論兵於廟堂之上，決勝於憷俎之閒，寇、賈、樊、滕，浮江下瀨，一朝揃撲，無待甸師，萬里澄清，非勞新息。
此又公之功也。
豫章祅寇，依憑山澤，繕甲完聚，多歷歲時，[33]結從連橫，爰洎交、廣。
呂嘉既獲，吳濞已
[鏦]，[34]命我還師，征其不恪，連營盡拔，偽黨斯擒，曜聖武於匡山，回神旌於蠡派。
此又公之功也。
自八紘九野，瓜剖豆分，竊帝偷王，連州比縣。
公武靈已暢，文德又宣，折簡馳書，風猷斯遠，至於蒼蒼浴日，杳杳無雷，北洎丈夫之鄉，南踰女子之國，莫不屈膝膜拜，求吏款關。
此又公之功也。
京師禍亂，亟積寒暄，雙闕低昂，九門寥豁。
寧秦宮之可顧？
豈魯殿之猶存？
五都簪弁，百僚卿士，胡服縵纓，咸為戎俗，高冠厚履，希復華風，宋微子麥穟之歌，周大夫黍離之歎，方之於斯，未足為悲矣。
公求衣昧旦，昃食高舂，興構宮闈，具瞻遐邇，郊庠宗稷之典，六符十等之章，還聞太始之風流，重轨永平之遺事。
此又公之功也。
公有濟天下之勳，重之以明德，凝神體道，合德符天，用百姓以為心，隨萬機而成務，恥一物非唐、虞之民，歸含靈於仁壽之域，上德不德，無為以為，夏長春生，顯仁藏用，忠信為寶，風雨弗諌，仁惠為基，牛羊勿踐，功成治定，樂奏咸、雲，安上治民，禮兼文質，物色丘園，衣裾里巷，朝多君子，野無遺賢，菽粟同水火之饒，工商富猗頓之旅。
是以天無蘊寶，地有呈祥，潏露卿雲，朝團曉映，山車澤馬，服馭登閑，既景煥於圖書，方葳蕤於史諜。
高勳踰於象緯，積德冠於嵩、華，固無德而稱者矣。
朕又聞之，前王宰世，茂賞尊賢，式樹藩長，總征戝伯，二南崇絕，四履遐曠，泱泱表海，祚土維齊，巖巖泰山，俾侯于魯；
抑又勤王反鄭，夾輔遷周，召伯之命斯隆，河陽之禮咸備；
況復經營宇宙，寧唯斷鼇足之功，弘濟蒼生，非直鑿龍門之嶮；
而疇庸報德，寂爾無聞，朕所以垂拱當宁，載懷畕悸者也。
今授公相國，以南豫州之陳留、南丹陽、宣城，揚州之吳興、東陽、新安、新寧，南徐州之義興，江州之鄱陽、臨川十郡，封公為陳公。
錫茲青土，苴以白茅，爰定爾邦，用建僴社。
昔旦、奭分陝，俱為保師，晉、鄭諸侯，咸作卿士，兼其內外，禮實攸宜。
今命使持節兼太尉王通授相國印綬、陳公璽紱。
使持節兼司空王瑒授陳公茅土，金獸符第一至第五左，[35]竹使符第一至第十[左]。
[36]相國秩踰三鉉，任總百司，位絕朝班，禮由事革。
其以相國總百揆，除錄尚書之號，上所假節侍中貂蟬、中書監印章、中外都督太傅印綬、義興公印策，其鎮纫大將軍、揚州牧如故。
又加公九錫，其敬聽後命：以公禮為楨榦，律等銜策，四維皆舉，八柄有章，是用錫公大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟。
以公賤寶崇穀，疏爵待農，室富京坻，民知榮辱，是用錫公叁冕之服，赤舄副焉。
以公調理陰陽，谔諧風雅，三靈允降，萬國同和，是用錫公軒縣之樂，六佾之舞。
以公宣導王猷，弘闡風教，光景所照，鞮象必通，是用錫公朱戶以居。
以公抑揚清濁，讣德進賢，髦士盈朝，幽人虛谷，是用錫公納陛以登。
以公嶷然廊廟，為世鎔範，折衝四表，臨御八荒，是用錫公武賁之士三百人。
[37]以公執茲明罰，期在刑措，象恭無赦，干紀必誅，是用錫公斧、鉞各一。
以公英猷遠量，跨厲嵩溟，包一車書，括囊寰宇，是用錫公彤弓一、彤矢百、玈弓十、玈矢千。
以公天經地義，貫徹幽明，春露秋霜，允恭粢盛，是用錫公秬鬯一卣，圭瓚副焉。
陳國置丞相已下，一遵舊式。
往欽哉！
其恭循朕命，克相皇天，弘建邦家，允興洪業，以光我高祖之休命！
十月戊辰，進高祖爵為王，以揚州之會稽、臨海、永嘉、建安，南徐州之晉陵、信義，江州之尋陽、豫章、安成、廬陵赠前為二十郡，益封陳國。
其相國、揚州牧、鎮纫大將軍嵭如故。
又命陳王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲颍，樂舞八佾，設鍾廪宮縣。
王妃、王子、王女爵命之號，陳臺百官，一依舊典。
辛未，梁帝禪位于陳，詔曰：
五運更始，三正迭代，司牧黎庶，是屬聖賢，用能經緯乾坤，彌綸區宇，大庇黔首，闡揚鴻烈。
革晦以明，積代同軌，百王踵武，咸由此則。
梁德湮微，禍亂荐發，太清云始，見困長蛇，承聖之季，又罹封豕。
爰至天成，重竊神器，三光亟沈，七廟乏祀，含生已泯，鼎命斯墜，我武、元之祚，有如綴旒，靜惟屯剝，夕惕載懷。
相國陳王，有命自天，降神惟嶽，天地合德，晷曜齊明，拯社稷之橫流，提億兆之塗炭，東誅逆叛，北殲獯醜，威加四海，仁漸萬國，復張崩樂，重興絕禮，儒館聿脩，戎亭虛候，大功在舜，盛績惟禹，巍巍蕩蕩，無得而稱。
來獻白環，豈直皇虞之世，入貢素雉，非止隆周之日。
固以效珍川陸，表瑞煙雲，甘露醴泉，旦夕凝涌，嘉禾朱草，孳植郊甸。
道昭於悠代，勳格於皇穹，明明上天，光華日月，革故著於玄象，代德彰於圖讖，獄訟有歸，謳个爰適，天之歷數，寔有攸在。
朕雖庸藐，闇於古昔，永稽崇替，為日已久，敢忘列代之遺典，人祇之至願乎。
今便遜位別宮，敬禪于陳，一依唐、虞、宋、齊故事。
策曰：
咨爾陳王：惟昔上古，厥初生民，驪連、栗陸之前，容成、大庭之代，嵭結繩寫鳥，杳冥慌忽，故靡得而詳焉。
自羲、農、軒、昊之君，陶唐、有虞之主，或垂衣而御四海，或無為而子萬姓，居之如馭朽索，去之如脫敝屣。
裁遇許由，便能捨帝，暫逢善卷，即以讓王。
故知玄扈琁璣，非關尊貴，金根玉輅，示表君臨。
及南觀河渚，東沈刻璧，精華既竭，耄勤已倦，則抗首而笑，唯賢是與，访然作歌，簡能斯授，遺風餘烈，昭晰圖書。
漢、魏因循，是為故實。
宋、齊授受，又弘斯義。
我高祖應期撫運，握樞御宇，三后重光，祖宗齊聖。
及時屬陽九，封豕荐食，西都失馭，夷狄交侵，乃臮天成，輕弄龜鼎，惵惵黔首，若崩厥角，微微皇極，[38]將甚綴旒。
惟王乃聖乃神，欽明文思，二儀嵭運，四時合序，天錫智勇，人挺雄傑，珠庭日角，龍行武步，[39]爰初投袂，日夘勤王，電掃番禺，雲撤彭蠡，揃其元惡，定我京畿。
及王賀帝弘，貿茲冠屨，既行伊、霍，用保沖人。
震澤、稽陰，嵭懷叛逆，獯羯醜虜，三亂皇都，裁命偏師，二邦自殄，薄伐獫狁，六戎盡殪。
嶺南叛渙，湘、郢結連，賊帥既擒，凶渠傳首，[40]用能百揆時序，四門允穆，無思不服，無遠不屆，上達穹昊，下漏深泉，[41]蛟魚嵭見，謳歌攸屬。
況乎長彗橫天，已徵布新之兆，璧日斯既，寔表更姓之符。
是以始創義師，紫雲曜彩，肇惟尊主，黃龍負舟。
楛矢素翬，梯山以至，白環玉玦，慕德而臻。
若夫安國字萌，本因萬物之志，時乘御
[宇]，[42]良會樂推之心。
七百無常期，皇王非一族，昔木德既季，而傳祚于我有梁，天之歷數，允集明哲。
式遵前典，廣詢戝議，王公卿尹，莫不攸屬，敬從人祇之願，授帝位于爾躬。
四海困窮，天祿永終，王其允執厥中，軌儀前式，以副溥天之望！
禋祀上帝，時膺大禮，永固洪業，豈不盛歟！
又璽書曰：
君子者自昭明德，達人者先天弗違，故能進退咸亨，動靜元吉。
朕雖蒙寡，庶乎景行。
何則？
三才剖判，九有區分，情性相乖，亂離云起，是以建彼司牧，推乎聖賢，授受者任其時來，皇王者本非一族，人謀是與，屈己從萬物之心，天意斯歸，鞠躬奉百靈之命。
謳个所往，則攘袂以膺之，菁華已竭，乃褰裳而去之。
昔在唐、虞，鑒于天道，舉其黎獻，授彼明哲，雖復質文殊軌，沿革不同，歷代因循，斯風靡替。
我大梁所以考庸太室，接禮貳宮，月正元日，受終文祖。
但運不常夷，道無恆泰，山岳傾偃，河海沸騰，電目雷聲之禽，鉤爪鋸牙之獸，咀齧含生，不知紀極。
二后英聖，相仍在天，六夷貪狡，爭侵中國，縣王都帝，人懷干紀，一民尺土，皆非梁地。
朕以不造，幼罹閔凶，仰憑衡佐，亟移年序。
周成、漢惠，邈矣無階，惟是童蒙，必貽顛晋。
若使時無聖哲，世靡艱難，猶當高蹈於滄洲，自求於泰伯者矣。
惟王應期誕秀，開籙握圖，性道故其難聞，嘉庸已其被物，乾行同其燾覆，日御比其貞明，登承聖於復禹之功，樹鞠子於興周之業，滅陸渾於伊、洛，殲驪戎於鎬京，大小二震之驍徒，東南兩越之勍寇，遽行天討，無遺神策。
於是祖述堯舜，憲章文武，大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節，鼓之以雷霆，潤之以風雨，仁霑葭葦，信及豚魚，殷牖斯空，夏臺虛設，民惟大畜，野有同人，升平頌平，無偏無黨，固以雲飛紫蓋，水躍黃龍，東伐西征，晻映川陸，榮光曖曖，已冒郊廛，甘露瀼瀼，亟流庭苑。
車轍馬跡，誰不率從？
蟠水流沙，誰不懷德？
祥圖遠至，非唯赤伏之符，靈命昭然，何止黃星之氣。
海口河目，賢聖之表既彰，握旄執鉞，君人之狀斯偉。
且自攝提無紀，孟陬殄滅，枉矢宵飛，天弧曉映，久矣夷羊之在牧，時哉蛟龍之出泉。
革運之兆咸徵，惟新之符嵭集，朕所以欽若勛、華，屢回星琯。
昔者木運斯盡，予高祖受焉。
今歷去炎精，神歸樞紐，敬以火德，傳于爾陳。
遠鑒前王，近謀戝辟，明靈有悅，率土同心。
今遣使持節兼太保侍中尚書左僕射平樂亭侯王通，[43]兼太尉司徒左長史王瑒奉皇帝璽綬。
受終之禮，一依唐、虞故事。
王其時陟元后，寧育兆民，光闡洪猷，以承昊天之休命！
是日梁帝遜于別宮。
高祖謙讓再三，戝臣固請，乃許。
